# bugs #4131: Struct-valued conditional expressions give an internal error in a return for z80 and stm8 and wrong values for mcs51

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4131/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. The mcs51 patches in the sixth and eighth comments concern the defect of #3885.
- Patch: [bugs-4131.patch](../../patches/bugs-4131.patch), commit [`695ce6c16`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/695ce6c16dc4935da000dc61b74c23eff8c04764). Apply after `bugs-4157-1.patch`, `bugs-3121.patch`, `bugs-3847.patch`, `bugs-3849.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For `return c ? a : b;` with struct operands, r17193 stops with the internal error and SIGSEGV of
the report for stm8 and z80. For mcs51 it compiles the statement without a diagnostic, and the
function returns wrong bytes in the small and large models and with `--stack-auto`.
`r = c ? f () : g ();` with functions that return a struct copies from a wrong address in every
mcs51 model.

## Cause

The value of a struct or union expression is the address of an object, and the output class in the
type of the operand gives the kind of that address. `geniCodeConditional` in `src/SDCCicode.c`
assigns the addresses of the second and the third operand to one temporary that has the type of
the conditional expression. The output class of that type does not have to match the objects. For
a call operand it is the code space, so mcs51 reads the value from code memory at the address of
the call's result object. For two objects in different address spaces, one kind of address cannot
be right. In a `return` statement the temporary becomes the operand of `RETURN`, and the code
generators return a struct from an object (#3847).

`geniCodeConditional` also evaluates the two operands as values. An operand `*p` or `a[i]` is read
through its address as a scalar, and the bytes that were read are used as the address (#4163,
#3857).

## Fix

The new `geniCodeStructAddress` evaluates an operand in the way the operand of `&` is evaluated
and casts the address to a generic pointer. When the expression has struct or union type,
`geniCodeConditional` calls it for both operands and gives the temporary the generic output class.
It does not allocate an object and does not add a copy. `ast2iCode` passes `return c ? a : b;` to
`geniCodeReturnStruct` from the patches for #3847 and #3849, which copies the value to its
temporary object.

`geniCodeStructAddress` calls `addLvaluereq` and `delLvaluereq` around the evaluation. With the
patch for #4054 applied first, the two calls are redundant. Without that patch, the tests for
#4163 and #3857 fail when the calls are absent.

The patch rewrites the comment at the check for error 172 in `genRet` of `src/mcs51/gen.c`, which
the first patch of #4157 adds. With this patch the front end does not produce an operand that the
check rejects.

The patch in the first and third comments allocates an object for each such expression and copies
to it the operand that the condition selects. It was read and was not applied.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4131.c.in` has the parts return, assign, and use with 51 assertions.
Its operands are variables, parameters, calls, an object in code memory, an automatic object, and
nested conditional expressions. On r17193, 30 assertions fail for mcs51-small, mcs51-large, and
mcs51-small-stack-auto. The assign part does not compile for mcs51-large-stack-auto, and the
return part does not compile for stm8 and ucz80. With the patch the test passes on the host, for
the six mcs51 variants, for stm8, and for ucz80.

Without the patch for #4054 and with earlier patches of the series applied, the regression suite
passes for mcs51-small, mcs51-large, mcs51-large-stack-auto, stm8, and ucz80, and the code size
and the simulated time of every other test are unchanged. valdiag passes for mcs51, mcs51-large,
mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. For mcs51 in the large model, programs with the operands `*p`,
`a[i]`, `w.m`, `p->m`, calls through a pointer, compound literals, and assignment expressions give
the output of the same source compiled with gcc. With the whole series applied, the regression
suite passes for the host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.

## Related

- #4163 and #3857 report operands of the form `*p`. This patch corrects them.
- #4054 has the patch that corrects an operand of the form `(e, *p)`. With this patch alone that
  operand is wrong, as `r = (e, *p);` is.
- #3885 has a patch that makes the change of the `getFreePtr` hunks in the two mcs51 patches of
  this ticket. The `genPointerPush` hunks of the second one are not in this series and were not
  tested.
- #4250, which the tenth comment names, reports the internal error for `return w.in;` and
  `return *p;`. The patch for #3849 is for these statements. The programs of #4250 were not run.
- With and without the patch, the compiler accepts `(c ? a : b).m = 1;`, `q = &(c ? a : b);`, and
  `(c ? a : b) = x;` without a diagnostic. The summaries of the open tickets do not show a ticket
  for this.
